idiom_name: Document + AbstractDocument over Map<String, Object> with HasX default-method traits
implementation_notes: This is the pattern's home form: Document declares the map-like contract, AbstractDocument implements it over one Map<String, Object> and finalises the accessors, and each trait - HasModel, HasPrice, HasParts - is an interface extending Document whose default methods read a key and cast. Noun classes such as Car are then just `extends AbstractDocument implements HasModel, HasPrice, HasParts`, so behaviour is composed per object without a hierarchy. Java 8 is the real floor: before default methods the traits had to be abstract classes, which forbids the union-of-traits trick. Nothing in the JDK replaces the structure, but Optional and Stream (for children) keep the casts out of the call sites.
pitfalls: The default accessors cast with (String)/(Number): a value stored under the wrong type throws ClassCastException at the read site instead of where it was written, so validate in a factory or write only through typed setters.

Views share the map by reference: wrapping it in Collections.unmodifiableMap while put() is still exposed turns the next write into an UnsupportedOperationException, and handing the same map to unrelated views lets one subsystem overwrite another's properties.
children() must rebuild views from the raw maps; storing view objects inside the document instead breaks write-through and serialisation.
Optional-returning accessors hide missing keys: a renamed key constant silently yields empty views rather than a compile error.

variants.name: Java 16+ record class implementing trait interfaces
variants.idiom_name: record Car(...) implements HasModel, HasPrice {} — compact noun types
variants.implementation_notes: Java 16 records can implement interfaces, so the noun type stays compact: `record Car(Map<String, Object> props) implements HasModel {}` — the record component is the constructor parameter, the trait accessor is inherited, and the record is implicitly final with auto-generated equals/hashCode/toString. A record that implements Document must still provide the document contract (for example, get delegates to props); records do not inherit storage behavior from AbstractDocument. A compact constructor body may validate the incoming parameter before the compiler performs the implicit component assignment, while a static factory is useful when construction must be restricted. This form is simpler than the abstract-class noun when targeting Java 16+.
pitfalls: The compact constructor body runs with the incoming component parameters before implicit field assignment; use it to validate the map, or use a static factory when construction policy must be hidden.
Records are implicitly final: they cannot be extended, and a view that needs subclass behaviour must be expressed as a regular class or as a sealed interface with record implementing types.
Records compare by component value (structural equality), not by identity — if the map is shared mutable state, equals may not be the right semantics.

variants.name: Jackson JsonNode tree with bound typed views
variants.implementation_notes: Jackson supplies the document half as a library: ObjectNode/JsonNode is a mutable, schema-less tree reached by name or index, and typed views are obtained by binding a subtree - treeToValue(node, Car.class) or readValue - onto a bean or record. The trait interfaces survive as separate bean types, one per consumer, sharing the same tree; use this when the document already arrives as JSON, and the hand-written Map<String, Object> form when documents are built in memory and no serialisation library should be in the core path.
pitfalls: unknown properties in the tree are ignored during binding unless FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES is enabled, so a typo in a view field silently reads nothing.
treeToValue copies data out of the tree: writes through the bound view no longer reach the document, unlike the shared-map form where the view writes through.
